text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers merge their code changes into a shared repository several times a day. The key to CI is automation. Every time code is pushed, a CI pipeline automatically starts a build. This means the software is compiled from the latest code without manual effort. After the build, the pipeline runs a series of automated tests. These tests check for bugs, errors, or broken features. The main benefit of CI is catching issues early. By detecting problems right after they are introduced, developers can fix them quickly and cheaply, before they grow into larger, more complex issues. This leads to more stable software and faster, more confident releases.
